usageNotes: Use this before authenticating a user against a PBS remote — it discovers which authentication realms (pam, pbs, openid, ldap, ad) are available on that host so you can present a valid realm choice. The `hostname` param must match the remote exactly as PBS expects it (including port if non-default, e.g. `pbs.example.com:8007`). Requires `System.Modify` on `/` in PDM, so API tokens scoped to narrower paths will be rejected.

examples.summary: List auth realms on a PBS remote at pbs.nightsquawk.tech

tips: If `fingerprint` is omitted and TLS verification fails, the call may be rejected — always supply the fingerprint when connecting to a self-signed PBS instance.
The `default` field on each returned realm indicates which realm PBS will use if none is specified at login; useful for pre-selecting the realm in a UI.
Realm type `pbs` is PBS's built-in user database; `pam` maps to the host OS users — both are always present on a standard PBS install.
